title: PENGUIN – PENicillin-allergy delabeling in German University hospital INpatients: A prospective multicentre study
summary:
Many people report having a penicillin allergy. However, in many cases this assumption is no longer accurate, or the original reaction was not a true allergy. Nevertheless, affected individuals are often treated with alternative antibiotics, which are usually broader in spectrum and may cause more side effects. This can result in longer hospital stays, more frequent readmissions, and overall poorer treatment outcomes. In addition, the increased use of such antibiotics contributes to the development of antibiotic resistance.

Studies show that around 95% of people with a documented penicillin allergy can actually tolerate penicillin. Using a structured approach (“delabeling”), it is therefore possible to reassess whether the allergy is still present in many patients. Validated methods are available to assess allergy risk. In patients with a low risk profile, this evaluation can also be performed by appropriately trained healthcare professionals outside the field of allergology.
conditions: Personal history of allergy to penicillin

interventions.name: PENGUIN is a multicenter, prospective observational study examining the use of a standardized algorithm and its impact in the context of routine clinical care. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with a history of penicillin allergy
- Current antibiotic therapy
- Planned inpatient treatment lasting more than 24 hours
Exclusion criteria:
- Under 18 years of age
- Pregnancy
- Use of antihistamines within the past 24 hours, or current use of corticosteroids at a dose exceeding 10 mg of prednisolone equivalent, or ongoing treatment with omalizumab
- Mastocytosis
- Idiopathic anaphylaxis/urticaria
- Current stay in the intensive care unit
